note_en: 得 links a verb or adjective to a comment on how it turns out: 长得不好 "grow poorly," 保持得比较合适 "be kept at a fairly suitable level." English puts an adverb after the verb ("grew badly"), but Chinese needs 得 as a bridge before the description. Don't confuse it with 的 (before nouns) and 地 (before verbs) — all three are pronounced de.
